key_insight: VoxProg turns natural-language instructions for placing objects in 3D scenes into executable programs over local voxel representations of scene surfaces. This gives language models a concrete way to express spatial relationships that instructions leave implicit.
problem_solved: Placing objects correctly in 3D requires more than understanding words: models must also construct geometric reference points and regions that are not explicitly specified.
method: Represent local scene surfaces using voxel views.
Use a language model to translate interpreted placement instructions into executable voxel programs.
Express geometric references and placement operations through those programs.
impact: The approach offers practitioners a programmatic bridge between language understanding and geometric reasoning for 3D object placement. The supplied abstract is truncated, so benchmark results and performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: spatial instruction → language model → voxel program → 3D object placement.

paper_title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
paper_authors: Zhichao Zhai, Menglei Zhao, Guikun Chen, Zihao Yan, Kanzhi Wu
